entries.description: Pinpoints the nearest authorized restroom for bus operator and field staff, using GPS and on-screen map.

entries.name: AC Transit Training and Education Department (TED) application
entries.description: This application supports the District's training operations for transportation and maintenance employees, primarily in the positions of Bus Operators and Heavy Duty Coach Mechanics (Apprentice and Journey), although the system supports new courses and apprenticeship programs.

entries.name: AC Transit Customer Relations application (CusRel)
entries.description: Public transit ticketing system for customer issues and feedback with: inter-departmental routing with notifications, department/person assigments, simple workflow, ticket searching, pre-canned reports, daily reminders and more.

entries.name: PTV Lines
entries.description: A cloud-based public transport software for line planning and public transport service optimisation

entries.name: RidePilot
entries.description: An open-source Computer Aided Scheduling and Dispatch (CASD) software system to meet the needs of small scale human service transportation agencies.

entries.description: , GitHub) - An R Shiny app to ingest ridership time series, and return seasonal, trend, and residual components according to STL methodology and forecasts including uncertainty based on those components. Sponsored by Metro Transit (Minneapolis-St. Paul).

entries.name: TBEST
entries.description: TBEST (Transit Boardings Estimation and Simulation Tool) is an effort to develop a multi-faceted GIS-based modeling, planning and analysis tool which integrates socio-economic, land use, and transit network data into a platform for scenario-based transit ridership estimation and analysis. Funded by the Florida Department of Transportation. Free to use but not open-source.

entries.description: A simple, spreadsheet-based tool for small demand-responsive transportation (DRT) services.

entries.name: "Legacy AVL system? It's okay, join the club." by Kurt Raschke
entries.description: Discussion of options for transforming legacy AVL system data into the GTFS-realtime format.

entries.name: "GTFS Best Practices now available!" by Sean Barbeau
entries.description: Discusses some of the challenges of an open data format like GTFS and the GTFS Best Practices that were launched in early 2017 to help address data quality.

entries.name: "What's new in GTFS-realtime v2.0" by Sean Barbeau
entries.description: Discuss the shortfalls in GTFS-realtime v1.0 and the improvements in v2.0.

entries.name: "AVL, CAD, and Real-Time Passenger Info for Beginners" by Tony Laidig
entries.description: Provides a general introduction to technology used to track vehicles.

entries.name: "Visualizing Better Transportation: Data & Tools" by Steve Pepple
entries.description: A collection of transportation-related data and tools for the San Francisco Bay Area and other cities in North America, originally collected and discussed at a 2018 Transit Week Event at ARUP in San Francisco.

entries.name: "How to use GTFS data to track transit vehicles in realtime" by Tom Camp
entries.description: Using GTFS and GTFS Realtime to provide continuous realtime updates.

entries.name: Tang et al. - "Ridership effects of real-time bus information system: A case study in the City of Chicago"
entries.description: Experiment in Chicago, IL showed modest increase in ridership when riders had access to real-time info via text message or email.

entries.name: Kay et al. - "When(ish) is my bus? User-centered Visualizations of Uncertainty in Everyday, Mobile Predictive Systems"
entries.description: Paper attempts to answr the question of "how do we communicate uncertainty in transit predictions?" Explains the problem, existing solutions and designs a better interface for letting users know when to arrive at the bus stop.

entries.name: Watkins et al. - "Where Is My Bus? Impact of mobile real-time information on the perceived and actual wait time of transit riders"
entries.description: Experiments in Seattl,e WA showed that riders perceived shorter bus wait times when they had access to real-time info via mobile apps.

entries.name: Brakewood et al. - “An experiment evaluating the impacts of real-time transit information on bus riders in Tampa, Florida”
entries.description: Controlled experiment in Tampa, FL showed that riders with access to real-time info via mobile apps perceived nearly 2 minute reduction in wait times compared to riders without real-time info. Riders with real-time info also had decreases in anxiety and frustration and better reception of agency.

entries.name: Brakewood et al. - "The impact of real-time information on bus ridership in New York City"
entries.description: Experiment in NYC showed that ridership increased on long routes when real-time info was made available to riders.

entries.name: Brakewood and Watkins - "A literature review of the passenger benefits of real-time transit information"
entries.description: (2018) - An overview of many different research studies looking at the benefits of real-time transit information.

entries.name: Higgins et al. - "Calculating place-based transit accessibility: Methods, tools and algorithmic dependence" (2022)
entries.description: Compares software tools for calculating accessibility by walking and public transit including ArcGIS Pro, Emme, R5R, and OpenTripPlanner.

entries.name: Aemmer et al. - "Measurement and classification of transit delays using GTFS-RT data"
entries.description: Presents a method for extracting transit performance metrics from a General Transit Feed Specification’s Real-Time (GTFS-RT) component and aggregating them to roadway segments. Used with Transit Vis, viewable here.

entries.name: APTA Policy Development and Research - Public Transportation Embracing Open Data
entries.description: APTA's discussion of the benefits and challenges of open transit data (a short summary of the below TCRP report).

entries.name: TCRP Synthesis 115 - Open Data: Challenges and Opportunities for Transit Agencies
entries.description: (2015) - A comprehensive report looking at the benefits and challenges of open transit data.

entries.name: TCRP Research Report 213: Data Sharing Guidance for Public Transit Agencies – Now and in the Future
entries.description: (2020) - A report designed to help agencies make decisions about sharing their data, including how to evaluate benefits, costs, and risks.
